summary:
Held 1 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — HPQ +12%, CHTR +8%, HONA +6%, AXON +6%, CDW +6%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 3 downside moves (LRCX -8%, AMAT -6%, SNDK -5%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: HPQ (+11.69%) — No confirmed catalyst found. Searches turned up no HPQ news dated 2026-11-27. The FQ4 results (revenue $16.0B, +9.3%) came out earlier, so this looks like a late reaction or a technical/sector move. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: HPQ is a mid/large-cap hardware name that no strategy's universe includes. It was also a thin, half-day post-Thanksgiving session with no pre-market news signal, so a news-reactive bot had no trigger either.

top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: HPQ is a mid/large-cap hardware name that no strategy's universe includes. It was also a thin, half-day post-Thanksgiving session with no pre-market news signal, so a news-reactive bot had no trigger either.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a daily 'unexplained gap' scan that admits any name up ≥8% on ≥2x average volume from the full liquid US universe (e.g. >$10B cap) to a watchlist, even when the name sits outside every strategy's static universe.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed catalyst found for 2026-11-27. Search only turned up older SpaceX mobile-partnership and Q2 rallies. Likely a rebound or sector move on the thin post-Thanksgiving half-day session.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CHTR is a mid-cap cable/broadband name with a heavily depressed price, which the universe filters apparently excluded. An unexplained, low-liquidity half-day jump would also fail any news-reactive trigger.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a daily 'unmapped mover' scan that admits any name up ≥+7% on ≥1.5× 20-day average volume to a watchlist, so strategies can evaluate it next session without widening the base universe.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found. Searches returned only stale 13F and analyst-target items. This was a thin, half-day session after Thanksgiving, so the move is likely technical or a Honeywell Aerospace spin-off flow effect.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. HONA is a newly spun-off large-cap aerospace name (Honeywell Aerospace, listed H2 2026) with little price history, so it was probably never added to any strategy's universe. Short-history indicators like RSI and average volume would also be unreliable.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an auto-onboarding rule so new listings and spin-offs with market cap above $10B join the momentum universe once they have 20 trading days of history (e.g. a min_history_days=20 parameter in the universe loader).

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 2026-11-27, so likely a technical or sector rebound. The stock is far below its ~$886 52-week high, and it was a thin half-day session after Thanksgiving.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: AXON is a mid/large-cap defense/public-safety tech name that no strategy includes. With no news catalyst, a news-reactive filter had nothing to trigger on, and a +6% half-day move on low volume would not clear momentum volume floors.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a liquid-large-cap 'discovery' bucket (e.g. S&P 500/400 names with a +5% close-to-close move on ≥1.5x 20-day average volume) to the momentum universe. Do not trade it on half-day sessions, where volume is distorted.

top_movers.catalyst: no obvious news catalyst found for 2026-11-27 — likely a technical / sector move on the thin post-Thanksgiving half-day session. Searches only surfaced earlier CDW jumps (Nov 4 earnings, June upgrade).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CDW is a mid-cap IT solutions/distribution name that no strategy includes. With no identifiable catalyst, a news-reactive bot had nothing to trigger on, and the shortened holiday session gave little time to build a signal.
top_movers.suggestion: No change warranted for this single move; if wanted, add mid-cap tech hardware/IT distributors to the momentum universe with a ≥+4% gap on ≥1.5× average volume filter, and skip half-day sessions.

top_movers.catalyst: No company-specific news found; EXE (Expand Energy, largest US gas producer) likely rose with a natural gas price rally (reports of a ~20-week high). Date of the rally is unverified.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: EXE is a ~$20B mid/large-cap Appalachian/Haynesville nat-gas E&P, and the energy-sector filter probably does not include it. The move was a commodity-beta move, not a catalyst the bot's signals would flag.
top_movers.suggestion: Add EXE (and peers like EQT, CTRA, AR) to the energy/commodity strategy universe, gated on a nat-gas front-month (NG=F) breakout of +3% or more. That lets the bot express gas strength through equities.

top_movers.catalyst: Continued chip-equipment selloff on MATCH Act / China export-curb fears, with AI-trade weakness. LRCX is the most China-exposed name (~35% of revenue). Exact 11/27 attribution is unconfirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: LRCX is a large-cap semiconductor-equipment name that no strategy includes. The drop was also a multi-day sector/policy slide, and 11/27 was a thin half-day session after Thanksgiving, so momentum and news filters had little to trigger on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap semi-equipment names (LRCX, AMAT, KLAC) to the mean-reversion universe, with a sector-wide gate that pauses entries while the group is down >5% for two or more days on policy news. Shorting isn't available, so this only avoids losses rather than capturing the move.

top_movers.catalyst: no obvious news catalyst found for 2026-11-27 — likely a technical or sector-wide memory/semis move on the thin post-Thanksgiving half-day session. Searches only returned undated or older MU selloff stories.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe (MU is a ~$590 large-cap semiconductor name not in any strategy's list). Only news-reactive-buzz-fade traded it, and a half-day drop with no headline gives it no buzz signal to fade.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap semis (MU, etc.) to the mean-reversion universe with a volume-normalised trigger on a ≤-5% close-to-close drop, discounting half-day sessions (e.g. 2.0× avg volume floor scaled by session length).

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 2026-11-27 (my search returned no AMAT item dated that day). Likely a semiconductor-equipment sector move on the thin post-Thanksgiving half-day session.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: AMAT is a large-cap semiconductor-equipment name that no strategy lists. A sector-wide, no-news drop on a half-day also gives news-reactive and gap filters nothing to trigger on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap semiconductor and semi-equipment names (AMAT, LRCX, KLAC) to the mean-reversion universe, with a min-volume floor so thin half-day sessions like the day after Thanksgiving are skipped. Treat a no-news sector drop as a dip-buy candidate only if the long side can take it.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed driver found for 11/27. Likely continued AI-hardware/memory-stock selling on a thin post-Thanksgiving half-day, following the Nov 10-13 NAND-share and Nvidia-CEO-exit sell-offs.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: SNDK is a recently spun-off, very volatile mid/large-cap memory/storage name that no strategy includes. A -5% move in a half-day session also falls below typical gap and volume-spike thresholds.
top_movers.suggestion: Add SNDK, and MU and WDC alongside it, to the momentum/news-reactive universe as a 'memory/NAND' sector basket, and gate it with a volatility-adjusted position size (e.g. ATR-scaled) rather than a flat cap.
